sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name the four sub-stages of childhood with ages.
questions.answer: Infancy (0–2), early childhood (2–6), middle childhood (6–11), adolescence (12–19).

questions.q: Name any three gross motor skills.
questions.answer: Crawling, standing, walking, running, climbing (any three).

questions.q: Name any three fine motor skills.
questions.answer: Grasping, pinching, holding a pencil, buttoning, cutting shapes (any three).

questions.q: Name the four stages of Piaget's cognitive development.
questions.answer: Sensori-motor, pre-operational, concrete operational, formal operational.

questions.q: Define (i) egocentrism; (ii) centration.
questions.answer: (i) Inability to see the world from another person's point of view. (ii) Focusing on one characteristic of an object and basing judgment on it.

questions.q: Fill in: (i) Development of empathy depends on ______ and ______ development. (ii) Playing without interaction is ______ play.
questions.answer: (i) cognitive; language. (ii) parallel.

questions.q: Fill in: (i) A child liked by some and disliked by others is called ______. (ii) An internal determiner of emotional development is ______.
questions.answer: (i) controversial. (ii) temperament.

questions.q: Name the four parenting styles.
questions.answer: Authoritarian, permissive, authoritative and neglectful (uninvolved).

questions.q: Name any two agents of socialization.
questions.answer: Parents, family, peers, school, religious institutions, mass media (any two).

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name the two sub-stages of the pre-operational stage and their ages.
questions.answer: Symbolic function (2–4 years) and intuitive thought (4–7 years). Features: mental images and egocentrism; questioning and centration.

questions.q: Identify the type of play: (i) children play beside each other without interaction; (ii) group pretend play; (iii) running, racing, climbing; (iv) learning to take turns.
questions.answer: (i) Parallel. (ii) Cooperative. (iii) Rough and tumble. (iv) Rough and tumble/cooperative play practising social rules.

questions.q: Identify the parenting style: (i) demanding, controlling; (ii) indulgent, non-demanding; (iii) firm with reasons; (iv) uncaring, low control.
questions.answer: (i) Authoritarian. (ii) Permissive. (iii) Authoritative. (iv) Neglectful.

questions.q: State the approximate age: (i) sitting alone; (ii) crawling; (iii) walking alone; (iv) riding a tricycle.
questions.answer: (i) 8 months. (ii) 9 months. (iii) 15 months. (iv) 3 years.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Differentiate gross motor from fine motor development.
questions.answer: Gross motor development is control of large muscles for crawling or walking; fine motor development is control of small muscles of hands and fingers for grasping or pinching.

questions.q: Why is the study of physical and motor development important?
questions.answer: It is the basis for personality, social and emotional development, helps bonding with the mother figure and gives mastery over the body.

questions.q: What is the 'language explosion' in early childhood?
questions.answer: Between 3 and 6 years the spoken vocabulary grows from about 900 words to 8,000–14,000 words and grammar develops.

questions.q: Describe the symbolic function sub-stage.
questions.answer: Children (2–4 years) make and store mental images, pretend play with absent objects, talk about people and places and role-play, but show egocentrism.

questions.q: What is empathy?
questions.answer: Understanding and sharing another's feelings; an important component of positive social behaviour that depends on cognitive and language development.

questions.q: What is socialization?
questions.answer: The process of acquiring norms, values and beliefs considered significant in a society.

questions.q: How does bullying affect victims?
questions.answer: Victims of bullies are often depressed and have lower self-esteem.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe physical development in middle childhood.
questions.answer: Growth is gradual until the puberty spurt at 11–13 years; girls are slightly shorter at 6–8 years but then taller and heavier, and their spurt comes earlier; children become stronger, faster and better coordinated and enjoy outdoor games.

questions.q: Explain motor development in early childhood.
questions.answer: Locomotion becomes graceful: a 3-year-old runs and jumps, a 4-year-old skips and catches a ball, 5–6-year-olds ride a bicycle with training wheels; fine skills include copying shapes, tying laces and self-care such as brushing teeth; hand preference begins.

questions.q: State the features of the pre-operational stage.
questions.answer: Use of symbols (words, images), pretend play and mental images, egocentrism, intuitive thought, centration and rapid language growth; thinking is not yet logical.

questions.q: State the achievements of the concrete operational stage.
questions.answer: Understanding of logical principles (conservation, transformation, seriation), better spatial reasoning and advanced language, but logical thinking is limited to real and concrete situations.

questions.q: Describe emotional development in early childhood.
questions.answer: Self-conscious emotions (shame, guilt) appear, children learn to modify emotions to suit situations, develop empathy and learn to control anger with guidance and role models.

questions.q: Describe parenting styles.
questions.answer: Authoritarian is demanding and controlling; permissive is indulgent; authoritative is firm and consistent with reasons; neglectful is uninvolved and uncaring. Authoritative parenting suits socialisation best.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe physical and motor development in early and middle childhood.
questions.answer: Early childhood: graceful locomotion, running, hopping, skipping, catching; fine motor skills grow from copying circles to squares and triangles, ties laces, self-care; hand preference. Middle childhood: slower growth until the spurt, gender differences (girls' spurt earlier), better strength, speed and eye-hand coordination, games with rules. Milestones are uniform in sequence but individuals differ in timing.

questions.q: Compare the pre-operational and concrete operational stages of Piaget.
questions.answer: Pre-operational (2–7): symbolic function, mental images, egocentrism, intuitive thought, centration, language explosion. Concrete operational (7–11): logical principles of conservation, transformation and seriation, improved spatial reasoning, logical thinking about real and concrete situations only, abstract concepts remain hard.

questions.q: Discuss socio-emotional development in childhood.
questions.answer: Early childhood: self-conscious emotions, emotion regulation, empathy, anger control, play from parallel to cooperative to rough-and-tumble. Middle childhood: social comparison, perspective taking, pride and shame, concealing emotions, moral judgment, gender differences, bullying, self-concept moving to traits and identity; peer acceptance supports self-esteem.

questions.q: Explain socialization and the influence of culture, parenting style and other factors.
questions.answer: Socialization transmits norms, values and beliefs through parents, family, peers, school, religion and media; the family dominates early childhood and peers and school middle childhood, when stereotypes form. Parenting styles are authoritarian, permissive, authoritative and neglectful; ethnicity and socio-economic status affect family size, education, income and child development.
